The cited evidence E1 discusses general corrosion/passivation effects of Si, Cr, Ni, Mo, Al, Ti in FeCoNiCr systems, not the specific Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy or its high-temperature oxidation behavior. E2 concerns oxidation of Nb-silicide-based alloys with Ti, Al, Cr, etc., and mentions pest oxidation, but does not address the proposed HEA or the mechanisms of scale cracking, spallation, or reduction-induced porosity. Thus, the key premise
premises: Selective oxidation of Cr and Ti drives oxide scale formation in the HEA.
In oxidizing atmospheres, the oxide scale becomes unstable (cracks, spalls) due to compositional inhomogeneity and thermal stresses.
In reducing atmospheres, partial reduction of the scale creates porosity that accelerates subsurface oxidation.
The degradation mechanism is surface-mediated and governed by diffusion and segregation of Cr and Ti.
The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports the role of Cr, Ti, and related elements in oxidation or corrosion of HEAs.
